title: Xanthe and the Promise
premise: When Casper Okafor's late grandmother leaves the family orchard to two names on one deed — his own and that of Xanthe Reyes, the woman who left him eleven years ago — neither can sell without the other's signature. Forced to spend a harvest season together restoring the dying trees, they excavate the misunderstanding that broke them: a letter Casper never sent and a secret Xanthe never asked about. As developers circle the orchard and Casper's daughter begins to hope for a family, both must choose between protecting their old wounds and telling the truth. In the end, they sign the deed over to a community land trust, keep the bookshop and the orchard alive side by side, and finally speak love in the present tense.
about_author: Felix Iversen is the pen name of a former orchard hand turned bookseller who writes love stories set in small towns where everyone remembers everything. He lives above a bookshop with an opinionated cat and a stubborn apple tree he refuses to give up on.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. While sorting his grandmother's affairs in the bookshop's back room, Casper discovers the orchard deed names both him and Xanthe Reyes as co-owners. His daughter Amara asks who Xanthe is, and he lies badly. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in grief, the past arriving by registered mail.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Counter
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe returns to town after her aunt's death, expecting to settle an estate quietly, and walks into Casper's bookshop to ask about the property. Eleven years of silence collapse into forty awkward minutes over a children's story hour. Beat: shock curdling into defensive anger.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. Neither will sign a quitclaim; Casper needs the sale money for the shop's leaking roof, Xanthe needs capital for her failing bakery in the city. They agree to one month of shared work before deciding. Beat: a truce built entirely out of resentment.

chapters.title: Pruning Lessons
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. First day in the orchard: half the trees are blighted, and Xanthe — raised here too — knows the old techniques better than he does. Amara trails Xanthe like a duckling, and Casper watches his daughter laugh in a way he hasn't seen since her mother left. Beat: reluctant admiration.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Helping clear the farmhouse, Xanthe finds a draft of the letter Casper wrote her the night she left — unsent, water-stained, unfinished. She pockets it instead of reading it fully, furious all over again at what it might have said. Beat: the wound reopened by evidence.

chapters.title: Saturday Story Hour
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Xanthe shows up uninvited to read at story hour, dazzling the children including Amara, who begs her to come back. A customer gossips about why Xanthe really left town years ago, and Casper realizes he never knew the whole story either. Beat: jealousy of the past and the present at once.

chapters.title: Developers at the Gate
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A development firm offers each of them a generous buyout — separately, hoping to divide them. Xanthe, needing bakery money, is tempted and ashamed. She overhears Casper refuse his offer outright. Beat: temptation versus loyalty to something not yet named.

chapters.title: What Amara Knows
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Amara, eight and merciless, asks Casper if Xanthe is 'the sad lady from your old photographs.' He admits they were once going to be married. That night he finds the missing letter gone from the floorboard and panics. Beat: fear that truth is leaking out sideways.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Cider House
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Rain traps them in the cider house; Xanthe produces the letter and demands answers. Casper explains the night she left: his grandmother told him Xanthe had taken the bakery job and ended it, and he was too proud to chase her. Both realize someone lied to them both. Beat: fury transforming into vertigo.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Searching the estate papers, Xanthe finds correspondence proving the grandmother intercepted letters and engineered the breakup, believing Xanthe would abandon Casper eventually. The revelation lands on the anniversary of the funeral. Beat: grief redirected at the dead, guilt at feeling it.

chapters.title: The Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Word spreads through the bookshop grapevine that the Okafor-Reyes orchard is for sale to developers. Loyal customers take sides; some blame Xanthe for leaving, others blame Casper for selling. Amara comes home crying from school. Beat: the cost of a private history made public.

chapters.title: One Good Harvest
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. With the buyout deadline looming, Xanthe proposes they run the orchard's cider weekend one last time before deciding anything. Working dawn to dusk, they fall into old rhythms — her laughing at his terrible ladder technique, him remembering how she takes her coffee. Beat: warmth sneaking past defenses.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. After the festival's success, a near-kiss under the oldest tree is interrupted by Amara's flashlight and a phone call: the developer has raised the offer and set a final date. Casper pulls back, terrified of repeating history. Beat: longing colliding with self-protection.

chapters.title: The Bakery Question
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe's city business partner gives an ultimatum: return with capital or lose the bakery. Torn, she tests the waters of staying — a lease inquiry, a conversation with the bank — and hates how much she wants it to work. Beat: hope as a risk she isn't sure she can afford.

chapters.title: Amara's Wish
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Amara, having pieced things together, writes a wish for the town wishing tree asking for 'Xanthe to stay forever.' Casper finds it and confronts his daughter gently, then himself harder. He realizes he's been making Amara pay for his caution. Beat: parental guilt and clarity.

chapters.title: The Signature Standoff
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Signing day arrives. At the lawyer's office, pen hovering, each waits for the other to flinch. Xanthe refuses first, declaring she won't be the one who abandons this place twice. Casper walks out without signing. Beat: defiance masking terror, the climax's fuse lit.

chapters.title: The Truth About the Night
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Digging further, Xanthe learns the full extent of the grandmother's interference — including a final letter delivered the morning Xanthe left, which she never received because Casper's grandmother kept it. She drives through a storm to bring it to him. Beat: urgency, vindication, tenderness.

chapters.title: Everything Unsaid
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Reading the eleven-year-old letter aloud in the rain-soaked bookshop, Casper finally hears his own young voice say what pride buried. They fight, weep, and forgive — not the grandmother, but themselves. Beat: catharsis; the emotional climax of the romance.

chapters.title: The Developer's Last Offer
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The developer plays his final card: a deadline of midnight and a threat to buy the adjoining land and strangle the orchard anyway. Casper and Xanthe, now aligned, race to find a third option before the town loses its heart. Beat: external stakes at maximum pressure.

chapters.title: The Land Trust Gambit
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe proposes transferring the deed to a community land trust, funded by townspeople, with the bookshop and a new bakery-café as anchors. The town rallies — even former rivals — and the developer's deadline passes with his offer unsigned. Beat: collective triumph, belonging made literal.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Weeks later: the orchard pruned and budding, the café framed, Amara teaching Xanthe's niece to climb the old tree. Casper asks Xanthe properly, in front of everyone at story hour, to stay — no deeds, no conditions. She says yes. Beat: joy earned, love spoken plainly.

chapters.title: The Promise Kept
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. One year on, at the orchard's spring blossom festival, Casper and Xanthe marry beneath the oldest tree while Amara reads the vows she helped write. The unsent letter is framed above the café counter. Beat: peace, continuity, memory transformed from burden into inheritance.
